title: IDFC First Bank Profit Surges 132% as AU Small Finance Bank Shows Recovery in Q1
excerpt: Both mid-tier Indian lenders posted strong Q1 FY27 results, with IDFC First Bank’s net profit more than doubling to ₹1,075 crore and AU Small Finance Bank reporting a 37% jump to ₹796 crore on improving asset quality.
body:
• IDFC First Bank’s Q1 FY27 net profit surged 132% year-on-year to ₹1,075 crore, driven by 21% NII growth and a sharp decline in provisions.
  • AU Small Finance Bank posted a 37% profit increase to ₹796 crore, with NIM expanding 47 basis points to 5.9% and gross slippages falling 22%.
  • Asset quality improved at both lenders — IDFC First Bank’s GNPA fell to 1.51% while AU SFB’s dropped to 2.10%, signaling the worst of the credit cycle may be behind them.
  • IDFC First Bank’s board approved raising up to ₹20,000 crore through equity and debt instruments to bolster capital.

Two of India’s closely watched mid-tier banks — IDFC First Bank and AU Small Finance Bank — reported strong first-quarter results on Saturday, each showing improved profitability and cleaner loan books after navigating a choppy credit environment over the past year.

IDFC First Bank: Profit More Than Doubles

IDFC First Bank’s net profit jumped 132% year-on-year to ₹1,075 crore in Q1 FY27, up from ₹463 crore in the year-ago quarter, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. The sharp improvement was underpinned by steady growth in core income and a meaningful reduction in provisioning costs.

Net interest income (NII) rose 21% to ₹5,972 crore, while other income — including fees, treasury gains, and recoveries from written-off accounts — climbed 23% to ₹2,128 crore. The bank’s net interest margin (NIM) expanded to 5.96% from 5.71% a year earlier.

Asset quality continued to improve. Gross non-performing assets (GNPAs) fell to 1.51% of gross advances at June-end 2026, down from 1.97% a year ago. Net NPAs declined to 0.44% from 0.55%.

“We are seeing strong business momentum... our asset quality continues to improve with Gross NPA of 1.51 per cent and net NPA of 0.44 per cent. Our provisions as a percentage of loans continues to come down.”

— V Vaidyanathan, MD and CEO, IDFC First Bank

Total loan assets grew 20.6% to ₹3,05,370 crore, while customer deposits rose 16.6% to ₹2,99,405 crore. The bank also received a ₹515 crore claim under the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU) and set aside an equivalent provision against potential monsoon or fuel-price volatility later in the year.

Looking to shore up its capital base, the board approved raising up to ₹7,500 crore through equity securities and up to ₹12,500 crore through debt instruments, giving the bank flexibility to tap capital markets as needed.

AU Small Finance Bank: Signs of a Turnaround

AU Small Finance Bank, which had been under pressure from stress in its microfinance portfolio, posted a 37% jump in net profit to ₹796 crore, up from ₹581 crore a year ago, according to Outlook Business.

NII surged 32% to ₹2,695 crore, while NIM expanded 47 basis points to 5.9%, helped by a 60-basis-point decline in the cost of funds to 6.48%. Total income rose 19% to ₹3,385 crore, though other income dipped 15% to ₹689 crore.

The Jaipur-headquartered lender showed clear improvement on the asset quality front. Gross slippages fell 22% to ₹798 crore, and the GNPA ratio dropped to 2.10% from 2.47%. Net NPAs improved to 0.76% from 0.88%. Provisions declined 30% to ₹371 crore, which included a one-time ₹23 crore provision to strengthen policies across microfinance, personal loans, two-wheeler, and EEFI portfolios.

The gross loan portfolio expanded 23% to ₹1,44,250 crore, supported by a 42% increase in disbursements. Deposits grew 24% to ₹1,57,727 crore, with the CASA ratio holding steady at 29%. The capital adequacy ratio remained comfortable at 18.9%, with Tier-I capital at 17.1%.

Universal Bank Transition and Tech Push

AU Small Finance Bank continues to work toward its transition to a universal bank after receiving the Reserve Bank of India’s in-principle approval in August 2025. During the quarter, it rolled out an AI-enabled gold loan origination platform and an agentic AI platform developed with Intellect Design Arena. More than 90% of transactions now flow through the bank’s AU 0101 app.

The board also elevated Yogesh Jain from Chief Operating Officer to Deputy CEO, effective July 25, strengthening the leadership bench ahead of the universal bank conversion.

What to Watch

For IDFC First Bank, the key question is whether it can sustain the improvement in credit costs after a turbulent FY26. The ₹515 crore monsoon provision suggests management is taking a cautious approach. For AU SFB, the declining slippages and NIM expansion indicate the worst of the microfinance stress may be behind it — but investors will watch whether the recovery holds through the monsoon season. Both banks trade at a premium to most public-sector peers, and continued earnings momentum will be critical to justifying those valuations.
nri_angle: IDFC First Bank and AU Small Finance Bank are widely held by NRI investors and both banks improved earnings signal strengthening fundamentals in India mid-tier banking sector.
